particle.description: Follows the topic the speaker wants to talk about.
particle.formation: [ A ] wa [ B ] desu. [ A ] is [ B ].
particle.example: Kinō wa ame datta 【昨日は雨だった】 It was rainy yesterday

particle.description: Identifies the specific subject performing the action or having the quality, often emphasizing the subject.
particle.example: Ame ga futte iru 【雨が降っている】 It is raining

particle.description: Indicates the object that receives the action of a transitive verb.
particle.example: Hon o yomu 【本を読む】 Read a book

particle.description: Indicates the destination of movement, a specific point in time, an indirect object, or the location where something exists.
particle.example: Tōkyō ni ikimasu 【東京に行きます】 I will go to Tokyo

particle.meaning: location of action / means / tool marker
particle.description: Specifies where an event or action occurs, or the method/means used to perform an action.
particle.example: Densha de gakkō e iku 【電車で学校へ行く】 Go to school by train

particle.description: Indicates the physical or metaphorical direction toward a goal or destination.
particle.example: Nihon e ikitai 【日本へ行きたい】 I want to go to Japan

particle.description: Connects multiple nouns exhaustively, or indicates companionship ("with someone").
particle.formation: [ Noun ] to [ Noun ] / [ Person ] to [ Verb ]
particle.example: Tomodachi to hanasu 【友達と話す】 Talk with a friend

particle.description: Replaces wa, ga, or o to indicate that the same statement applies to another subject or object.
particle.example: Watashi mo gakusei desu 【私も学生です】 I am also a student

particle.description: Indicates the starting point in space or time, or acts as a conjunction expressing a reason or cause.
particle.example: Ku-ji kara hajimaru 【九時から始まる】 Starts from nine o’clock

particle.meaning: until / up to / as far as
particle.description: Indicates the terminus, limit, or destination in time or distance.
particle.example: Tōkyō kara Kyōto made 【東京から京都まで】 From Tokyo to Kyoto

particle.description: Used in comparisons to denote the reference point ("more than [Noun]").
particle.example: Inu wa neko yori ōkii 【犬は猫より大きい】 Dogs are bigger than cats

particle.description: Placed at the end of a sentence to seek agreement, confirmation, or show empathy with the listener.
particle.example: Ii tenki desu ne 【いい天気ですね】 Nice weather, isn’t it?

particle.description: Placed at sentence end to give new information or assert conviction with emphasis.
particle.example: Ashita wa yasumi desu yo 【明日は休みですよ】 Tomorrow is a holiday, you know!

particle.description: Transforms a statement into a question at the end of a sentence.
particle.example: Kore wa nan desu ka 【これは何ですか】 What is this?

particle.description: Connects two nouns where the first modifies the second, indicating possession or relationship.
particle.example: Watashi no hon 【私の本】 My book
